rules.DryWatch: 3-month rain at or below 75% of normal and soil moisture in the driest 25% for this month
rules.FloodWatch: rain at or above 150% of normal this month on soil already in the wettest 25%
rules.SlopeWatch: a hill district (10% or more of its land steeper than 15 degrees in NASA SRTM elevation data) where soil is in the wettest 25% and rain is at or above 130% of normal
rules.ground_wetness: GLDAS root-zone soil moisture when it is no more than a month old; GLDAS runs about 3 months behind, so for recent months the rank of the last 3 months of rain against the same months in 2001-2025 stands in for it

hill_rule.source: NASA NASADEM_HGT v001 (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission), 30 m

rule.source: NASA GPM IMERG daily rain (Early for the newest days, about 4 hours after each day ends; Late once it arrives), averaged over each district, with NBRO's 24-hour rainfall steps (75, 100, 150 mm)
rule.1: Yellow, be aware: 75 mm or more in the last day, or the district is on SlopeWatch or FloodWatch
rule.2: Amber, be ready: 100 mm or more in the last day, or 75 mm on ground that is already soaked (a Watch is on)
rule.3: Red, act now: 150 mm or more in the last day, or 100 mm on ground that is already soaked
rule.drought: DryWatch is shown as Level 1 (save water)

towns.source: NASA GPM IMERG daily, Early then Late (0.1 degree), and NASADEM 30 m terrain, per Divisional Secretariat division
